options.C: Working in high-altitude environments for many hours
options.D: Consuming excessive amounts of dietary protein supplements

explanation: Professionals who sit for long hours often experience increased scrotal temperatures, which harms sperm quality. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: A patient going through alcohol withdrawal begins to show severe tremors, high blood pressure, and confusion. What is the immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Discontinue all monitoring to avoid agitating the patient further
options.B: Implement seizure precautions and monitor vitals closely
options.C: Leave the patient alone in a quiet room to rest undisturbed
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the unit to burn off energy

explanation: Severe alcohol withdrawal can lead to dangerous seizures and delirium tremens, making close vital sign tracking and safety precautions essential. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is another common name for primary polycythaemia?

options.A: Polycythaemia vera
options.B: Secondary erythrocytosis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Aplastic anemia

explanation: Primary polycythaemia is also called polycythaemia vera. It happens right inside the bone marrow stem cells!

question: Why is having a skilled birth attendant present during delivery so important?

options.A: They make antenatal visits unnecessary
options.B: They can quickly spot and manage emergencies like heavy bleeding
options.C: They guarantee the baby won't cry at birth
options.D: They prevent the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Exactly! Skilled attendants have the training to handle sudden delivery complications and save lives before things get out of hand.

question: In a patient health history, what do we mean by the 'chief complaint'?

options.A: The primary reason the patient is seeking care, in their own words
options.B: The surgical history from the patient's childhood
options.C: The final medical diagnosis written by the attending physician
options.D: A complete list of every prescription medication the patient takes

explanation: Spot-on! The chief complaint is simply the main trouble or symptom that brought the patient to the clinic, written using what they tell you.

question: A client taking long-term NSAIDs for joint pain reports stomach upset and dark, tarry stools. What should you do first?

options.A: Advise the client to double the fluid intake immediately
options.B: Report the findings promptly to the healthcare provider
options.C: Suggest taking the medication on an entirely empty stomach
options.D: Reassure the client that dark stools are a normal side effect

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a telltale sign of bleeding in the gut (GI bleed), a serious side effect of long-term NSAID use. Always report this right away!

question: Which sign tells you a mixed lotion should be thrown away immediately?

options.A: A label showing it was mixed three days ago
options.B: Visible separation or discoloration
options.C: A smooth and uniform texture throughout
options.D: A slight cooling sensation upon skin contact

explanation: If the cream separates or changes color, it means it has gone bad and is no longer safe to use. You're doing great!

question: What happens during an 'ascending infection' in the female reproductive system?

options.A: Pathogens move upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes
options.B: Viruses migrate from skin lesions down to the regional lymph nodes
options.C: Fungi multiply rapidly on the external vulva and travel to the bladder
options.D: Bacteria travel through the bloodstream directly to the heart valves

explanation: An ascending infection is just germs traveling upward—moving past the cervix and into the upper reproductive organs where they can cause serious trouble.

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the plotting of the active phase on a standard partograph typically begin?

options.A: 10 centimeters
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 7 centimeters
options.D: 1 centimeter

explanation: The active phase and routine partograph plotting traditionally commence once the cervix reaches 4 centimeters of dilation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: What is a major part of helping a pregnant client make a practical birth plan?

options.A: Arranging transportation and identifying the place of delivery
options.B: Purchasing expensive imported toys for the nursery
options.C: Choosing the exact college the child will attend later
options.D: Deciding whether the mother will return to work in a week

explanation: A good birth plan solves logistics! Knowing how she will get to the hospital and exactly which health facility she is going to prevents dangerous delays during labor.

question: You cannot feel a dying patient's radial pulse at the wrist. What should you do next as the nurse?

options.A: Call the doctor immediately to start IV fluids
options.B: Apply a warm water bottle to their hands
options.C: Pump the blood pressure cuff higher on their arm
options.D: Check a central pulse like the carotid or femoral

explanation: When peripheral circulation gets weak, wrist pulses fade first. Checking a central pulse helps you accurately check the remaining heart activity. You're building great clinical instincts!

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop germs from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all household laundry
options.B: Taking daily multivitamins
options.C: Proper hand hygiene
options.D: Wearing rubber gloves outdoors

explanation: Never underestimate good old handwashing! It washes away germs before they have a chance to get inside you or others.

question: Which common fungus frequently causes yeast infections on the vulva?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Candida albicans
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Candida albicans is a fungus that normally hangs out on our bodies harmlessly, but when conditions are right, it can overgrow and cause that familiar itching and irritation. Keep up the great revision!

question: Your syringe driver beeps with an occlusion alarm. What is the very first thing you should check?

options.A: If the room lights are turned on brightly
options.B: Whether the extension tubing is kinked or clamped
options.C: Whether the pharmacy has new medication orders
options.D: If the patient's blood pressure is stable

explanation: Exactly right! Tracing the tubing to look for a bend, twist, or closed clamp usually fixes an occlusion alarm in seconds.

question: What is a major benefit of a midwife engaging with traditional leaders and birth attendants?

options.A: Training them to perform major cesarean sections independently
options.B: Encouraging early antenatal booking and formal facility delivery
options.C: Taking over the administration of local government offices
options.D: Eliminating the need for any primary health care clinics

explanation: Partnering with community figures helps build trust and directs pregnant women toward skilled birth attendance at health facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h5)

question: What makes intravenous therapy risky regarding how fast drugs act?

options.A: The slow onset of therapeutic effects
options.B: Unpredictable absorption from the gut
options.C: Total immunity to local tissue irritation
options.D: The rapid irreversibility of drug action

explanation: You're doing great! Once a medicine goes straight into the vein, you cannot take it back out. That's why we always double-check our doses—reactions happen fast and are harder to reverse than oral pills.

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy?

options.A: Painful blisters forming exclusively around the mouth
options.B: Rapid darkening of the skin over the entire body
options.C: Severe itching on the palms and soles without an initial rash
options.D: Thick crusting sores spreading across the scalp

explanation: Take note of this one for the ward! Intense itching on hands and feet without a rash can mean liver acid backup (cholestasis) and needs quick medical attention.

question: Why must you shake a suspension bottle vigorously right before pouring a dose?

options.A: To cool down the liquid inside the glass container
options.B: To evenly redistribute settled solid drug particles
options.C: To check if the outer safety seal is broken
options.D: To create air bubbles that make the drug taste better

explanation: Shaking mixes the active medicine back into the liquid so the patient gets the right dose, not just flavored water!

question: A patient has high blood insulin levels, but their body cells fail to absorb glucose properly due to faulty receptor signaling. What is this scenario called?

options.A: Extracellular deficiency
options.B: Hormone upregulation
options.C: Insulin resistance
options.D: Second messenger failure

explanation: Insulin resistance occurs when target cells stop responding properly to insulin despite adequate or elevated levels in the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h6)

question: A patient with untreated hypothyroidism is admitted with a body temp of 33°C, a very slow pulse, and low consciousness. What is happening?

options.A: Thyrotoxic storm
options.B: Addisonian crisis
options.C: Myxedema coma
options.D: Diabetic ketoacidosis

explanation: You're doing great! Severe, slow-moving hypothyroidism that drops body temperature and causes unresponsiveness is called a myxedema coma.

question: Why do healthcare providers often use the umbilical vein for emergency drugs in the delivery room?

options.A: It provides fast, reliable access to the central circulation
options.B: It avoids the risk of fluid infiltration into tissues
options.C: It prevents the need for any sterile preparation
options.D: It allows continuous blood pressure monitoring only

explanation: The umbilical vein is wide, easy to find in an emergency, and leads straight to the main bloodstream, getting life-saving drugs where they need to go fast.

question: Which of these is a well-known long-term health complication of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhanced hormonal balance during adolescence
options.B: Permanent immunity to sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Obstructed labor and chronic pelvic infections
options.D: Complete elimination of menstrual cramps

explanation: FGM leaves behind scar tissue that can cause long-term pain and make childbirth terribly dangerous later in life. It's a key practice public health nurses actively campaign against.

question: Why might a doctor order a CT scan after a biopsy confirms vulval cancer?

options.A: To measure the exact resting heart rate of the patient
options.B: To find out if the patient has a history of skin allergies
options.C: To check if the cancer has spread to lymph nodes or other organs
options.D: To determine if the patient has a secondary urinary tract infection

explanation: Well done! Imaging tests help us stage the cancer by showing if abnormal cells have travelled to nearby lymph nodes or further away.

question: Which structure is known as the natural pacemaker of the heart?

options.A: Sinoatrial node
options.B: Bundle of His
options.C: Purkinje fibers
options.D: Atrioventricular node

explanation: The sinoatrial node sets the normal pace for the heart because it depolarizes faster than any other conducting tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: What receptor combination is the trademark of second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics?

options.A: Dopamine and serotonin receptor blockade
options.B: Opioid and adrenergic receptor agonism
options.C: GABA and norepinephrine enhancement
options.D: Histamine and acetylcholine stimulation

explanation: Remember: first-gen mostly blocks dopamine, but second-gen (atypical) agents block both dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors at the same time.

question: An elderly patient has a weakened cough reflex. What major complication are they at risk for?

options.A: Sudden enlargement of the vocal cords
options.B: Spontaneous rupture of the diaphragm
options.C: Lower respiratory tract infections
options.D: Complete collapse of the nasal passages

explanation: Spot on! When older adults can't cough well, mucus stays trapped in the airways, becoming a breeding ground for bacteria and leading to chest infections.

question: Why might a standard health pamphlet fail if you just hand it out to any community without checking?

options.A: Only medical doctors are legally allowed to read pamphlets
options.B: Pamphlets are universally banned by the ministry of health
options.C: It may ignore the unique setting, culture, and lifestyle of the group
options.D: Printed paper cannot carry any medically accurate information

explanation: Brilliant insight! One size doesn't fit all in nursing. Care must always fit the specific culture and lifestyle of the people we serve.

question: What is the best first step for a unit manager when an unexpected error happens on the ward?

options.A: Hide the incident report from the hospital board
options.B: Lead an investigation to find the root cause
options.C: Immediately dismiss the nurse on duty
options.D: Close the entire ward to new admissions

explanation: Spot on! Quality care is all about finding out *why* something went wrong so the system can be fixed, rather than just pointing fingers at individuals.

question: Why is watching a patient walk (their gait) such an important part of a nursing assessment?

options.A: It replaces the need to check vital signs during an admission
options.B: It measures the exact level of calcium circulating in the blood
options.C: It provides a definitive laboratory diagnosis for osteoporosis
options.D: It reveals hidden balance issues and weaknesses in weight-bearing joints

explanation: A quick look at how someone walks can tell you a lot about their balance and joint strength before they take a nasty fall!

question: Why do physical signs of puberty usually show up long after the internal hormonal changes have already started?

options.A: Because the skin blocks hormones from reaching the rest of the body early on
options.B: Because bones refuse to lengthen until a person turns twelve years old
options.C: Because internal chemical signals must build up and stimulate target organs over time
options.D: Because children eat too many processed foods before growing up

explanation: Well done! Hormones start working quietly behind the scenes in the brain way before you can actually see any physical changes on the outside.

question: What makes an ectopic pregnancy a major concern for a woman who has had a tubal ligation?

options.A: Sperm can easily bypass the surgical blockages and dissolve the uterine lining.
options.B: If pregnancy occurs, the blocked tube increases the chance the egg implants outside the uterus.
options.C: Hormonal imbalances caused by the surgery force eggs to grow in the abdominal wall.
options.D: The scar tissue prevents the ovaries from releasing any hormones at all.

explanation: While overall pregnancy rates after tubal ligation are very low, any pregnancy that does happen carries a much higher risk of being ectopic, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h6)

question: What position should your patient be in when you are inserting a nasogastric tube?

options.A: Lying on the left side (Sims position)
options.B: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position
options.C: Head tilted downward (Trendelenburg)
options.D: Flat on the back (supine)

explanation: Sitting the patient straight up aligns their throat nicely, making it much easier and safer to slide the tube down. Great job!

question: If a patient stays in bed for a very long time due to a degenerative disease, what happens to their joints and muscles?

options.A: Permanent joint contractures and muscle wasting
options.B: Enhanced muscle mass and core strength
options.C: Rapid increase in overall bone mineral density
options.D: Instantaneous thickening of joint cartilage

explanation: Use it or lose it! Without movement, muscles shrink (wasting) and tissues tighten up into fixed positions.

question: When should instruments be checked for cleanliness and damage?

options.A: Directly after removal from the autoclave
options.B: Only when the surgeon complains about a tool
options.C: As soon as the items arrive dirty from the ward
options.D: After cleaning and before packaging

explanation: Staff inspect instruments right after they are washed and dried. This ensures no hidden dirt or broken parts slip through before they are wrapped up.

question: How do teenagers normally show they are trying to be more independent from their parents?

options.A: Refusing to make any decisions on their own
options.B: Questioning family rules and testing personal boundaries
options.C: Completely cutting off all communication with adults
options.D: Seeking total approval for every daily action

explanation: Testing boundaries and questioning authority is a totally normal way teenagers practice thinking for themselves and building autonomy.

question: What does the 'T' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Tumor size and extent
options.B: Tissue toxicity
options.C: Total body weight
options.D: Treatment schedule

explanation: In the TNM system, T evaluates the size and direct extent of the primary tumor, N assesses lymph node involvement, and M checks for distant metastasis. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the best immediate step for a clinic facing a sudden stockout of syringes?

options.A: Tell nursing staff to wash and reuse standard syringes
options.B: Borrow supplies from a nearby cooperating facility
options.C: Stop providing all injection treatments indefinitely
options.D: Wait patiently for the next quarterly delivery

explanation: Brilliant! Emergency borrowing between friendly neighboring clinics bridges the gap safely without resorting to dangerous reuse.

question: What financial headache do many NGOs face all the time?

options.A: Excessive government funding with no rules
options.B: Funding instability due to shifting donor priorities
options.C: Making too much profit from free clinics
options.D: Paying excessive taxes on humanitarian donations

explanation: Spot on! NGOs often worry about money because donors frequently change which regions or medical issues they choose to fund. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h5)

question: Who is famous for introducing the 'total pain' concept in palliative care?

options.A: Cicely Saunders
options.B: Elisabeth Kubler-Ross
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Spot on! Dame Cicely Saunders pioneered modern hospice care and taught us that pain is more than just physical—it includes emotional, social, and spiritual parts too.

question: Which symptom in a newborn or young infant is a clear indication for urgent hospital referral?

options.A: Mild sneezing during the early morning hours
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin on day four
options.C: Inability to breastfeed or drink anything
options.D: Sleeping for six hours straight at night

explanation: An infant who cannot feed is showing a dangerous sign of severe illness that requires immediate hospital evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why can taking an oral azole antifungal cause other routine medications to become toxic in the body?

options.A: Azoles inhibit liver enzymes that normally break down other drugs
options.B: Azoles force the kidneys to reabsorb all circulating prescription drugs
options.C: Azoles bind directly to other medications in the stomach and trap them
options.D: Azoles destroy the protein carriers that transport vitamins in the blood

explanation: Azoles slow down the liver's cleanup crew (P450 enzymes). With the crew on break, other drugs pile up in the blood and can become toxic.

question: When inserting a rectal suppository, past which structure must it go to stay in place?

options.A: Internal anal sphincter
options.B: The sigmoid colon
options.C: The external skin folds
options.D: The ileocecal valve

explanation: You want to push it just past that internal sphincter muscle. If you don't, the body's natural reflex will push it right back out. Good nursing touch makes all the difference!

question: A patient tells you they stopped taking their daily allopurinol because their toe stopped hurting. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Suggest they double the dose of allopurinol whenever they eat red meat or drink alcohol
options.B: Confirm that they no longer need any medication since the pain has completely gone away
options.C: Explain that the medication must be taken daily to keep uric acid low and prevent future attacks
options.D: Advise them to switch to taking ibuprofen every time they feel a slight twinge in the toe

explanation: You've got it! Allopurinol isn't a painkiller for a single attack—it's a daily maintenance routine. Stopping it lets uric acid climb right back up and brings the pain back.

question: A clinic nurse counts the total number of pregnant women who received iron tablets today. What is this count called?

options.A: Impacts
options.B: Outputs
options.C: Inputs
options.D: Assumptions

explanation: Outputs are the direct, immediate results of your work today—like the count of services delivered or items given out.

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe nursing action after a patient returns from an MRI where they received mild sedation for anxiety?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in a low position with rails up
options.B: Allowing the patient to walk unaccompanied to the bathroom
options.C: Monitoring vital signs until the sedation wears off
options.D: Checking for signs of allergic reactions to any contrast dye

explanation: Sedated patients are at a high risk for falls and dizziness, so they should never walk alone until fully recovered. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is a CT scan particularly useful for musculoskeletal disorders?

options.A: It clearly reveals complex fractures and deep bone issues.
options.B: It safely treats severe joint inflammation without surgery.
options.C: It provides real-time video of moving muscle fibers.
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical assessments.

explanation: The layered, cross-sectional imaging of a CT scan allows healthcare providers to see intricate bone structures and hidden fractures that regular x-rays often miss. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why should you NEVER make a patient vomit after they swallow kerosene?

options.A: It makes the poison taste much worse on its way back up
options.B: It can cause the chemical to enter the lungs and cause aspiration pneumonia
options.C: It immediately neutralizes all medications given in the hospital
options.D: It causes instant blindness in both eyes

explanation: Well done! Coming back up, kerosene can easily slip into the windpipe and lungs, causing severe chemical pneumonia.

question: Which main body fluid is collected during a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Synovial fluid
options.B: Lymphatic fluid
options.C: Venous blood
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Spot on! The procedure draws cerebrospinal fluid from around the spinal cord to help doctors run diagnostic tests.

question: Your patient suddenly gasps and feels dizzy halfway through draining fluid. What should you do first?

options.A: Document the total amount of fluid drained so far
options.B: Notify the provider immediately and stop the drainage
options.C: Administer the prescribed oral pain medication right away
options.D: Ask the patient to sit up straight and take deep breaths

explanation: Safety first! Sudden dizziness or coughing can mean a rapid fluid shift or a lung issue, so pause the procedure and alert the doctor right away.

question: A 14-year-old pregnant girl is in active labor with a narrow pelvis. What major complication is she most at risk for?

options.A: Chronic autoimmune kidney failure
options.B: Obstructed labor and potential fistula formation
options.C: Sudden adult-onset diabetes mellitus
options.D: Permanent hearing loss from high blood pressure

explanation: Exactly! An immature pelvis makes it hard for the baby to pass safely, leading to long, blocked labor and tissue injury. Early care can save lives here.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to approach health promotion with teenagers?

options.A: Ignoring lifestyle habits until adulthood is reached
options.B: Reporting all experimental behavior to the local police
options.C: Using strict scare tactics to prevent bad habits
options.D: Providing non-judgmental guidance and open education

explanation: You got it! Teens respond best when we listen without scolding them, offering honest education and support they can trust.

question: What is an early or forced marriage?

options.A: Any wedding that takes place without religious approval
options.B: A marital arrangement organized strictly by government officials
options.C: A union where one or both parties are under 18 without full consent
options.D: Any marriage occurring between individuals from different tribes

explanation: Spot on! Early and forced marriage means minors are pushed into a union without giving free and wise personal consent. As nurses, protecting the young is key!

question: A patient with long-term diabetes complains of blurry vision and dark spots. Which eye problem should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute glaucoma
options.B: Retinal detachment
options.C: Nuclear cataracts
options.D: Diabetic retinopathy

explanation: Well done! Years of high blood sugar can damage the small blood vessels in the retina, making diabetic retinopathy a very common cause of vision changes.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the main sections found on a standard partograph?

options.A: Progress of labour evaluation
options.B: Fetal condition assessment
options.C: Maternal condition monitoring
options.D: Surgical site infection rates

explanation: The partograph focuses purely on active labour. It breaks down into three clear sections: the baby's condition, how labour is progressing, and the mother's vital signs.

question: Why is a drug antagonist often compared to a broken key in a lock?

options.A: It fits the space but does not open the door
options.B: It falls out of the keyhole immediately after insertion
options.C: It destroys the lock mechanism permanently
options.D: It opens the door faster than the original key

explanation: Just like a snapped key fills up the keyhole so no other key can fit, an antagonist sits in the cell receptor without activating it. Simple and easy to picture!

question: A hospital manager checks patient charts to see if a new pain relief guide is working well. What goal does this support?

options.A: Patient self-monitoring of symptoms
options.B: Personal communication between doctors
options.C: Immediate bedside nursing handover
options.D: Quality improvement and research

explanation: Correct! Looking back at charts helps the hospital find ways to upgrade patient care and nursing protocols.

question: What is the main purpose of having clear referral pathways for children with special needs?

options.A: Ensuring only doctors make decisions about the child
options.B: Increasing paperwork for family members
options.C: Directing the child to the correct specialist without delay
options.D: Reducing the number of available hospitals

explanation: Clear referral steps ensure that patients move smoothly to the exact specialists they need without getting lost in the system.

question: How does great teamwork between doctors, nurses, and pharmacists improve safety?

options.A: By ensuring all team members share critical concerns and catch dosing errors early
options.B: By reducing the total number of medications any patient is allowed to take
options.C: By allowing nurses to bypass doctors and prescribe medications independently
options.D: By shifting all legal responsibility for medication errors onto the pharmacist

explanation: Open communication builds a safety net around the patient. When we talk to each other, mistakes get caught early!

question: A nurse treats a high blood pressure patient living in a neighborhood with poor food access. What is the best all-round approach?

options.A: Provide medication while also connecting the patient to local nutritional resources and food programs
options.B: Focus solely on writing prescriptions without discussing the patient's diet
options.C: Tell the patient to only purchase expensive imported foods from distant supermarkets
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until their blood pressure normalizes

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Good treatment means handing out medicine while also helping the patient find practical food support right in their community.

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement in osteomyelitis?

options.A: To fuse the adjacent joints together permanently
options.B: To stretch the limb to make it longer
options.C: To replace all marrow with synthetic polymers
options.D: To remove dead and infected bone tissue

explanation: Debridement is basically a clean-up operation where the surgeon scrapes away all the dead, infected bone that antibiotics alone can't reach.

question: How does tuberculosis mostly spread from one person to another?

options.A: Ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products
options.B: Direct contact with contaminated skin lesions
options.C: Inhalation of airborne droplet nuclei
options.D: Sharing eating utensils and drinking cups

explanation: When someone with active TB coughs or sneezes, tiny droplets float into the air. If others breathe them in, they can catch the infection too.

question: What happens if a traction rope slips out of its pulley groove?

options.A: The patient's blood pressure will drop rapidly
options.B: The pulling force on the extremity is lost
options.C: The fracture will heal twice as fast
options.D: Skin breakdown will immediately disappear

explanation: If the rope rubs against the bed frame instead of the pulley, the mechanical pull stops and the traction won't work. Good thing you're checking your equipment!

question: Why is the immune system so important for our survival?

options.A: It regulates the normal daily temperature of the human body
options.B: It digests food nutrients inside the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: It controls the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: It protects the body against harmful microorganisms in the environment

explanation: Spot on! Think of your immune system as your body's personal security guard, constantly working behind the scenes to shield you from harmful germs.

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient taking oral prednisone to protect their stomach?

options.A: Take the medication on an empty stomach.
options.B: Crush the pills and dissolve them in juice.
options.C: Take the medication right before going to bed.
options.D: Take the medication with food or milk.

explanation: Correct! Steroids can be harsh on the gut lining, so taking them with food, milk, or a meal helps prevent stomach upset.

question: A patient with suspected Addison's disease is at high risk for which dangerous electrolyte imbalance?

options.A: Hypercalcemia resulting from excess bone breakdown
options.B: Hyperkalemia due to aldosterone deficiency
options.C: Severe hyponatremia caused by water intoxication
options.D: Hypokalemia caused by excessive renal excretion

explanation: Aldosterone is the hormone that normally tells our kidneys to flush out extra potassium. Without enough aldosterone, potassium builds up in the blood, leading to risky high levels (hyperkalemia).

question: What is the first emergency medicine to give if a newborn's heart rate stays under 60 despite breathing support and chest compressions?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is our go-to emergency drug to help jumpstart the heart rate and improve heart muscle squeeze during severe bradycardia.

question: Why is knowing the location of the dorsal penile nerves important during a circumcision?

options.A: It controls the blood flow to the entire lower abdomen
options.B: It guides where to give a local nerve block for pain relief
options.C: It helps prevent accidental removal of the urethral opening
options.D: It ensures the scrotal skin heals without any scarring

explanation: You've got this! Doctors inject local numbing medication near these dorsal nerves on top of the penis to block pain signals effectively and keep the baby comfortable.

question: What kind of special precautions do you need when caring for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Droplet precautions
options.D: Standard precautions only

explanation: Spot on! TB germs float around in tiny particles in the air, so you'll need specialised protection like an N95 respirator mask.

question: Who typically leads a peer-led HIV support group?

options.A: A licensed medical doctor or surgeon
options.B: A hospital laboratory technician
options.C: A veteran community member living with HIV
options.D: A government health policy maker

explanation: Peer-led groups are guided by individuals who share the lived experience of managing the condition successfully. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: How can chronic (long-term) inflammation lead to a cervical polyp?

options.A: It destroys local nerve endings
options.B: It directly causes malignant cell transformation
options.C: It triggers abnormal tissue proliferation over time
options.D: It blocks the production of estrogen

explanation: Think of it like skin getting a callus from constant friction. Ongoing irritation makes the cervical tissue grow extra cells, forming a polyp over time.

question: Why is continuous, long-term monitoring so essential when caring for patients with degenerative conditions?

options.A: It completely stops the underlying genetic mutation from spreading
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees the patient will regain full physical strength
options.D: It helps catch slow, steady declines and new complications early

explanation: Because these diseases creep up slowly over time, keeping a close eye on the patient helps us catch new problems right away and step in to help.

question: What is the most important part of sexual consent?

options.A: Long-term plans for marriage and children
options.B: Financial stability of both individuals involved
options.C: Voluntary and clear agreement from all parties
options.D: Approval from parents or legal guardians

explanation: Spot on! True consent must always be given freely, clearly, and without any pressure or force.

question: Your patient is nervous and shivering, and their ECG comes out looking super jagged. What should you do first?

options.A: Remove the chest electrodes and document that the test is impossible to perform
options.B: Immediately call the emergency response team for a suspected cardiac arrest
options.C: Apply extra conductive gel to the chest wall and increase the machine gain
options.D: Reassure the patient, provide a warm blanket to stop shivering, and repeat the tracing

explanation: Shivering makes muscle tremors that mess up the screen. Just warm them up, help them relax, and run it again!

question: Why does the body need to metabolize drugs, especially fat-soluble ones?

options.A: To make fat-soluble drugs easier for the kidneys to excrete
options.B: To completely prevent medications from entering the bloodstream
options.C: To make all drugs stay inside fatty tissues forever
options.D: To turn every drug into a permanent fat-soluble storage form

explanation: Think of it this way: our kidneys love water-soluble stuff. If a drug is too fatty, the kidneys just let it circulate back. Metabolism changes it so the kidneys can easily flush it out in urine! You've got this.

question: What is a key part of a safety plan made for someone who has experienced violence?

options.A: Quitting your job right away without any money saved
options.B: Confronting the abuser face-to-face in a public place
options.C: Knowing safe places to go and packing important documents
options.D: Avoiding all contact with healthcare workers and social workers

explanation: Well done! A practical safety plan helps someone leave quickly if danger gets worse, including knowing where to find shelter and keeping vital papers ready.

question: What makes primary health care nurses so crucial for disease surveillance?

options.A: They are responsible for funding national health budgets.
options.B: They manufacture all the vaccines used in the country.
options.C: They write the international guidelines for disease control.
options.D: They interact directly with patients daily and spot early signs of disease.

explanation: As frontline nurses, you are the eyes and ears of health surveillance because you see the patients first every single day!

question: Why should you wait fifteen minutes to take a patient's temperature if they just rushed in from the hot sun?

options.A: To give the patient time to calm down during triage
options.B: To make sure the disposable probe cover doesn't melt
options.C: To let the thermometer warm up its internal sensors
options.D: To let their skin temperature adjust to the indoor air

explanation: Hot or cold weather temporarily changes surface skin temperature. Giving them a few minutes inside ensures your reading is accurate.

question: Why is serious injury to the medulla oblongata considered immediately life-threatening?

options.A: It controls vital autonomic functions like breathing and heart rate
options.B: It produces all visual images for the eyes
options.C: It stores all long-term memories for daily living
options.D: It coordinates voluntary balance during walking

explanation: The medulla houses the respiratory and cardiac centers that keep a person breathing and maintain blood pressure automatically. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is a common health intervention that voluntary agencies use to protect pregnant women and infants?

options.A: Providing heavy industrial machinery
options.B: Issuing international travel passports
options.C: Building commercial shopping complexes
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated mosquito nets

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is a big threat in Nigeria, so handing out treated nets to mothers and babies saves countless lives.

question: A patient with Type AB-positive blood needs emergency red blood cells and none of their exact type is available. Which blood type can they safely receive?

options.A: Any blood type
options.B: Only Type O-negative
options.C: Only Type A-positive
options.D: Only Type AB-positive

explanation: Type AB-positive individuals are universal recipients for red blood cells because their blood does not contain antibodies against A, B, or Rh antigens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h5)

question: Where do water-soluble (peptide) hormone receptors usually sit?

options.A: On the outer cell membrane
options.B: Attached directly to cellular DNA
options.C: Inside the cell nucleus
options.D: Floating freely in the cytoplasm

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't slip through the oily cell membrane, they have to catch their receptors right on the outer surface of the cell.

question: What does it mean when a cancer cell is called 'poorly differentiated'?

options.A: The cancer cells look very different from normal tissue cells
options.B: The tumor cells have stopped growing completely
options.C: The cells are surrounded by a thick protective capsule
options.D: The mass is unable to attract a blood supply

explanation: Well done! 'Differentiated' means looking like the original tissue. Poorly differentiated cells have lost their specialized look, which usually means the cancer is more aggressive.

question: What is fluid balance in the human body?

options.A: Drinking the exact same amount of water every day
options.B: Water entering the body equals water leaving it
options.C: Having more electrolytes than water in the blood
options.D: Keeping all body water inside the blood vessels

explanation: Fluid balance simply means intake matches output over a given period to keep the system stable. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h1)

question: Your patient cries out in sharp pain as you inflate the catheter balloon. What is your very first move?

options.A: Stop inflation immediately and check if the catheter is still in the urethra
options.B: Push the catheter in harder to reach the proper depth
options.C: Inject the remaining water quickly to finish the procedure
options.D: Administer an oral painkiller and continue inflating

explanation: Stop right away! Pain during balloon inflation usually means the balloon is stuck inside the narrow urethra instead of resting safely in the bladder.

question: What makes the foramen ovale snap shut at birth?

options.A: Higher pressure in the left atrium compared to the right atrium
options.B: The physical tie placed on the umbilical cord
options.C: Contraction of the heart muscle due to cold air
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's core body temperature

explanation: As blood floods back from the newly working lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure pushes the little flap of the foramen ovale shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: Which major structural change happens in the lungs of someone with emphysema?

options.A: Thickening of the pleural space with fibrous scar tissue
options.B: Destruction of alveolar walls and loss of lung elasticity
options.C: Permanent blockage of the main pulmonary artery by clots
options.D: Excessive production of watery fluid inside the pleural cavity

explanation: You got it! Emphysema breaks down the walls of the air sacs and destroys the elastic fibers, making it hard for the lungs to bounce back when breathing out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h4)

question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Art and science
options.B: Administration and finance
options.C: Theory and politics
options.D: History and geography

explanation: Nursing combines the emotional and human connection of art with the empirical clinical knowledge of science to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: What exactly is a hospital-acquired complication?

options.A: An expected outcome of chronic disease progression
options.B: A negative health event developing during hospital care
options.C: An illness the patient had before admission
options.D: A normal side effect of curative surgery

explanation: You've got this! These are issues that pop up because a patient is in the healthcare setting or undergoing treatment, rather than being there when they first arrived.

question: What directly causes barotrauma in a patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Lack of early physical therapy and leg movement
options.B: Inadequate hand hygiene by the nursing staff
options.C: Bacterial infection growing in the endotracheal tube
options.D: High airway pressure or excessive lung volume

explanation: Too much pressure or blowing the lungs up like an over-inflated balloon can pop delicate air sacs, causing air to leak where it shouldn't.

question: What is the main reason a nurse performs an eye irrigation?

options.A: To flush out chemicals or foreign bodies from the eye
options.B: To deliver antibiotic eye drops for a bacterial infection
options.C: To permanently dilate the pupil for a detailed eye exam
options.D: To measure the exact intraocular pressure of the globe

explanation: Great job thinking practically! Irrigation uses a steady stream of fluid to wash away dangerous substances or particles before they hurt the eye tissues. You've got this!

question: Why might a hospital find it hard to use primary nursing instead of team nursing?

options.A: Team nursing requires every single staff member to hold a master's degree.
options.B: Primary nursing completely eliminates the need for any communication with doctors.
options.C: Team nursing prevents nurses from ever talking to patients or families.
options.D: Primary nursing requires a larger proportion of registered nurses, which increases staffing costs.

explanation: Primary nursing needs lots of qualified Registered Nurses to give that individualized care, which can be expensive for hospital management compared to mixing in more junior staff.

question: Why do we place absorbent material inside the secondary packaging of a medical specimen?

options.A: To cushion the glass tubes against heavy outside vibration
options.B: To soak up all the liquid if the primary tube breaks
options.C: To keep the biological specimen frozen during long flights
options.D: To absorb moisture from the humid clinic room air

explanation: It's a built-in safety net! If a tube cracks, the absorbent material traps the fluid so it never leaks outside.

question: Which emergency during the third stage of labor requires an immediate hospital transfer?

options.A: Mild postpartum fatigue
options.B: Normal placental separation
options.C: Transient shivering after birth
options.D: Severe postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery can quickly become life-threatening. Stop the bleeding and get the mother to the hospital fast!

question: What color and type of container is standard for collecting used sharps in the ward?

options.A: Puncture-resistant yellow container
options.B: Transparent white polythene bag
options.C: Green cardboard carton
options.D: Open black plastic bucket

explanation: You got it! Sharps need hard, puncture-proof containers—usually yellow with biohazard signs—to keep everyone safe from needle sticks.

question: Why are the secretions of the accessory glands necessary for reproduction?

options.A: They help sperm survive the acidic female reproductive tract
options.B: They trigger the production of new testosterone in the testes
options.C: They prevent the testes from overheating during physical activity
options.D: They physically carry the egg down the fallopian tube

explanation: Seminal fluid contains alkaline substances and nutrients that protect sperm against harsh, acidic environments. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the main limitation of relying solely on national laws to stop harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Courts are legally forbidden from hearing domestic abuse cases
options.B: Laws cannot change deep social beliefs without community engagement
options.C: Law enforcement officers are exempt from handling family matters
options.D: International treaties always override local criminal statutes

explanation: Legislation provides penalties, but if the community still values the tradition, practices simply go underground. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: What is the main difference between primary and secondary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Secondary dysmenorrhoea never involves cramping in the lower abdomen
options.B: Primary dysmenorrhoea is caused by abnormal growths in the uterus
options.C: Primary dysmenorrhoea only affects women over forty years of age
options.D: Secondary dysmenorrhoea is caused by an underlying pelvic pathology

explanation: Primary dysmenorrhoea has no structural cause, whereas secondary dysmenorrhoea stems from a specific disease process like fibroids or endometriosis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for the physiological anemia seen during pregnancy?

options.A: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass
options.B: Red blood cells are actively destroyed at a much faster rate
options.C: Frequent blood tests deplete the iron stores of the mother
options.D: Dietary iron is completely blocked from being absorbed in the gut

explanation: Because plasma volume expands much faster and larger than the actual red blood cell count, the blood becomes more diluted, which registers as a lower hemoglobin concentration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support such an important part of nursing care for infertility?

options.A: Psychological counseling guarantees a successful pregnancy
options.B: Infertility causes significant grief, anxiety, and relationship strain
options.C: Patients with infertility rarely experience physical symptoms
options.D: It completely replaces the need for medical treatments

explanation: Trying to conceive can be an emotional rollercoaster. Compassionate nursing support is vital to help patients keep their spirits up.

question: Why is assessing family dynamics an important first step for a nurse?

options.A: It determines the exact date the patient contracted the virus
options.B: It helps identify who can serve as the primary care partner
options.C: It proves whether the family has a history of viral infections
options.D: It legally binds the family to pay for all future drugs

explanation: Brilliant! Understanding relationships inside the home helps the nurse find the most supportive relative to assist with care.

question: When calculating the incidence of a disease, what goes on top (the numerator)?

options.A: The number of new cases developed during a period
options.B: The entire population living in the community
options.C: The number of patients who recovered completely
options.D: The total number of people who died from old age

explanation: Great job! The numerator in an incidence formula always focuses strictly on the newly diagnosed cases.

question: What are the three classic signs of bacterial meningitis?

options.A: Tremors at rest, slow movement, and rigid limbs
options.B: Chronic cough, chest pain, and night sweats
options.C: Sudden weight gain, hair loss, and dry skin
options.D: Severe headache, high fever, and stiff neck

explanation: Keep this classic triad in mind: headache, fever, and a stiff neck (nuchal rigidity). Whenever you see these together in a test or ward, think meningitis!

question: A nurse notices a frayed electrical cord on an infusion pump. What is the immediate action to take?

options.A: Leave a sticky note on the screen and use it for one patient
options.B: Remove the pump from service and tag it for repair
options.C: Wrap the frayed area tightly with standard office tape
options.D: Plug it into a different wall socket to test the current

explanation: Frayed electrical cords pose severe shock and fire risks, so faulty equipment must be immediately taken out of use and labeled for biomedical maintenance. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which symptom pattern is most typical for someone with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)?

options.A: Severe sudden constipation that leads straight to a bowel blockage
options.B: Painless bleeding from the rectum every time they pass stool
options.C: Constant bloody stools accompanied by high fevers and weight loss
options.D: Recurrent abdominal pain tied to changes in stool frequency and form

explanation: Well done! IBS is diagnosed when belly pain keeps coming back and is linked with changes in how often and how hard or loose their stools are.

question: Why is it dangerous to use the total volume of a multi-dose liquid bottle when calculating a single dose?

options.A: Total volume measurements are always written in incorrect metric units
options.B: Liquid medications lose their potency once the safety seal is broken
options.C: The total volume is the container size, not the active drug concentration per dose
options.D: Manufacturers change the concentration levels daily inside the same bottle

explanation: Exactly! If you use the whole bottle's volume instead of the concentration per unit, you could accidentally cause a massive overdose.

question: For how many months should an infant be exclusively breastfed (no other food or water)?

options.A: First three months
options.B: First six months
options.C: First twelve months
options.D: First two weeks

explanation: Correct! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives a baby all the food and immune defense they need without needing water or other foods yet.

question: Why do we tell patients to elevate a sprained ankle above the level of the heart?

options.A: It increases arterial blood flow to speed up ligament fiber regeneration
options.B: Elevation prevents the development of systemic blood clots in the leg
options.C: Gravity helps drain excess fluid and reduce swelling at the injury site
options.D: It relaxes the calf muscles so the bone fracture can heal properly

explanation: Elevation uses gravity to pull extra fluid away from the injured area, helping to bring down that painful swelling.

question: Which parts of the body usually show the earliest physical signs of a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Internal organs like the liver, kidneys, and pancreas
options.B: Rapid-turnover tissues like skin, hair, and mucous membranes
options.C: Dense connective tissues like cartilage and deep ligaments
options.D: Structural elements like cortical bone and long bones

explanation: Tissues that grow and shed quickly need a constant supply of nutrients, so they show signs of trouble first when supplies run low.

question: Which medication class is most commonly associated with causing orthostatic fainting?

options.A: Antacids
options.B: Antihypertensives
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Analgesics

explanation: Medications that lower blood pressure can sometimes drop it too far, especially when standing up, leading to fainting. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which health issue puts an HIV-positive patient into WHO Clinical Stage 4?

options.A: A normal CD4 count with no physical complaints
options.B: Kaposi sarcoma or severe opportunistic infections
options.C: Recurrent common colds and mild skin rashes
options.D: Persistent generalized swollen lymph nodes only

explanation: Spot on! Stage 4 involves severe illnesses and indicator conditions that mark advanced HIV disease (AIDS). [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a strict 'no-go' (absolute contraindication) for putting in an IUD?

options.A: Mild iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Having had a past cesarean section
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: Confirmed or suspected pregnancy

explanation: Never place an IUD if a woman is already pregnant! It can cause serious complications, severe infection, or miscarriage.
